open_questions.body: Which of the following statements best describes your approach to using AI in a professional context?

open_question_options.body: I have limited to no experience with AI tools and am not yet convinced of their practical benefits in a work environment.
I consistently use AI tools to improve my personal efficiency, validate the quality of my own work, and build simple automations for my individual tasks.
I proactively improve team efficiency by designing, building, and maintaining multi-step automated workflows, and I actively share these solutions with my team.
I strategically redesign core operations by architecting scalable AI systems, coaching others to raise their AI skills, and identifying work that can be entirely eliminated by AI.

open_questions.body: Engineering has two options for a new onboarding flow. The full redesign removes every friction point for Evas but takes 10 weeks. An 80/20 version fixes the biggest drop-off step and ships in 3 weeks. What do you do?

open_question_options.body: Ship the 80/20 version now and plan the full redesign as phase 2.
Go with the 80/20 version, since it covers most Evas, and revisit the rest if complaints come in.
Commit to the full redesign and push engineering to find a faster way to deliver it.
Ask data to calculate the conversion impact of both options before deciding.
Let engineering decide, since they own delivery and feasibility.

open_questions.body: You are redesigning how your product function works, and AI agents will be part of it. What is your approach?

open_question_options.body: Run a pilot in one team and keep the current structure everywhere else until the results are proven.
Ask each team to try AI tools and share what they find.
Hire AI specialists into each team to lead the change.
Map the work, give AI agents the routine parts, keep people for judgment, and size teams on that basis.
Outsource the routine work to an external provider.

open_questions.body: Users are dropping off during onboarding because of a KYC step owned by Compliance Operations. The fix needs Product, Compliance and Engineering. What do you do?

open_question_options.body: Set up a working group with all three teams and agree on shared KPIs.
Agree on a clear RACI first, so every department owns its own part.
Pass it to Compliance Operations, since they own KYC, and offer support.
Decide on the fix, get the other leads aligned, and drive it to delivery.
Escalate to the management board to assign one owner.

open_questions.body: A regulator asks you to explain a past product decision within a week, and the documentation is incomplete. What do you do?

open_question_options.body: Ask for a short extension so the response is complete and accurate.
Reconstruct what you can, respond on time, state the gaps openly, and fix how decisions get documented.
Let Legal lead the response, with your team providing input.
Respond on time, but only with the parts you can fully document.
Ask the original team to recreate the missing documents.
